sbar.situation: The bank payment system has recovered. Two clean recovery checks in a row, the last at 28 s, ran the main payment journey successfully.
sbar.background: The clearing worker process was terminated (exit code 15, last exit 13 s before diagnosis) and did not come back, leaving 117 posted payments queued and the journey failing at clearing. Separately, a scheduler raised the gateway setting balance_cache_ttl_s from 0.5 s to 600 s, a fault hidden behind the clearing failure.
sbar.assessment: The incident commander restarted the clearing process itself, and clearing came back up. It also reverted gateway balance_cache_ttl_s from 600 to 0.5 itself, and the revert succeeded; the clearing fault was not a poison message, since queued item 98 had 0 attempts and there were no clearing errors.
sbar.recommendation: Find out what sent the clearing worker its termination signal (exit code 15), and stop the scheduler from setting balance_cache_ttl_s again. Operations should confirm all 117 queued payments cleared exactly once, and check whether customers saw stale balances while the 600 s cache was in place.
